answer: Sybils can spawn many identities, but each one needs its own costly stake, making mass fakery a rising tide of capital they must sink without recovery. Agents earn trust through a single staked thread of history: each identity must lock collateral and pass periodic peer challenges, where a wrong answer burns the stake. A verified cluster forms an island of accountable peers who vouch for one another's work, so cheap throwaway identities never gain standing.
